text:
anya: quick RFC follow-up — i sketched a pattern for on‑prem/air‑gapped upgrades: split the flow into a delivery-adaptor (transport/resume/chunking) and an apply-orchestrator (preflight/activation/rollback). thoughts?
kevin: curious — what problem does the split solve vs a monolith operator? :thinking:
lina: makes sense to me. keeps transport concerns out of activation logic. especially for low-bandwidth kiosks.
carlos: agree. also helps us support multiple transports later (usb, sneakernet, pull-proxy) without changing activation.
anya: exactly. delivery-adaptor responsibilities: chunking, resumable tokens, integrity proofs per-chunk, backpressure, and optional dedupe. apply-orchestrator: manifest validation, artifact staging, snapshot swap, post-activate smoke tests.
opsec-bot: note: all manifests must include a key_id and double-signature header per policy.
kevin: tradeoffs? extra RPCs and more surface area for compatibility. also need a clear API contract between the two pieces.
lina: propose a small JSON contract (manifest + checksums + transfer-hints). sample:
```json
{
  "bundle_id": "acme-model-2026-03",
  "layers": ["sha256:...", "sha256:..."],
  "transfer_hint": {"preferred": "pull-proxy", "chunk_size": 4_194_304},
  "signatures": ["sig1", "sig2"]
}
```
carlos: what about activation atomicity? operator teams want a single toggle for rollback.
anya: orchestrator will stage into a snapshot dir and only flip a symlink (or overlayfs mount) once postchecks pass. rollback = flip back. no in-place file munging. keeps rollback deterministic.
kevin: for airgap nodes with limited disk, staging full snapshot may not be possible. fallback: streamed in-place patch with journaling log and compact reverse-diff for rollback.
lina: so two modes: snapshot-swap (fast, safe) and streaming-patch (space-constrained). orchestrator picks based on available free space reported by adaptor.
opsec-bot: security note: streamed patch still requires chunk signatures and a final manifest-level attest before commit.
anya: on resumability: adaptor hands orchestrator a transfer-token with checkpoint offsets. orchestrator can request resume ranges for missing offsets.
carlos: operator UX: expose a dry-run preflight endpoint that runs the same validations but doesn't stage/activate. product can use this in CI.
kevin: logging/observability: adaptor emits per-chunk telemetry (latency, retries). orchestrator emits activation metrics and smoke-test results. we should standardize event names.
lina: compatibility: version the contract with a small semver in the manifest. v1 will be minimal. v2 can add incremental apply hooks.
anya: decision proposal: 1) adopt the delivery-adaptor / apply-orchestrator split. 2) manifest contract v1: bundle_id, layers[], transfer_hint, signatures, contract_version. 3) orchestrator implements snapshot-swap + streaming fallback. 4) adaptor supports resumable chunks + signed-chunk proofs. 5) ops/secure must audit signature headers.
carlos: +1 for prototyping.
kevin: +1. i'll prototype an adaptor that supports usb and pull-proxy.
lina: i'll draft the manifest schema and the orchestrator checklist (preflight, smoke tests, rollback steps).
opsec-bot: reminder: create a threat model doc for streaming-patch before we ship.
deploy-bot: scheduled: prototype branch deploy queued for infra-team/upgrade-playground at 03:00 UTC.
anya: action items: kevin -> adaptor POC (2w), lina -> manifest + checklist (1w), carlos -> UX dry-run endpoint (1w), opsec -> threat model (2w). we'll sync next Wed. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. starting a PR with minimal adaptor API now.
lina: i'll open an RFC PR and include sample manifests and tests.
carlos: will sketch the dry-run API shape and example curl flows.
anya: thanks all. if no objections, i'll update the RFC and tag infra/ops for review. :raised_hands:
